27+814.58smodel_callimplement{"cassette_key": "075706b258d97984", "cost_usd": 1.354215, "from_replay": false, "input_tokens": 8398, "latency_seconds": 535.468528, "model": "claude-opus-5", "output_tokens": 52489, "parsed": {"files": [{"content": "fastapi==0.115.6\nstarlette==0.41.3\npydantic==2.10.4\nuvicorn==0.32.1\nhttpx==0.28.1\npytest==8.3.4\n", "path": "requirements.txt"}, {"content": "# URL Shortener\n\nA small FastAPI + SQLite URL shortener: create short links, follow them, read click\nstatistics. Link creation is rate limited; every other endpoint is not.\n\n## Endpoints\n\n| Method | Path | Purpose |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `GET` | `/health` | Liveness probe. Touches no user data and no database. |\n| `POST` | `/api/links` | Create a short link. Rate limited (see below). |\n| `GET` | `/api/links/{code}/stats` | Click statistics for a code, including `expired`. |\n| `GET` | `/{code}` | 307 redirect to the stored target URL (not listed in OpenAPI). |\n\n### Create a link\n\n```\nPOST /api/links\nContent-Type: application/json\n\n{\"url\": \"https://example.com/a/very/long/path\", \"expires_in_seconds\": 3600}\n```\n\n`expires_in_seconds` is optional (omit it for a link that never expires) and `code`\nis an optional custom short code (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}`). The response is `201`:\n\n```json\n{\n \"code\": \"aB3dE7f\",\n \"short_url\": \"http://localhost:8000/aB3dE7f\",\n \"target_url\": \"https://example.com/a/very/long/path\",\n \"created_at\": \"2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z\",\n \"expires_at\": \"2024-01-01T01:00:00.000000Z\"\n}\n```\n\n### Expired links\n\nExpiry is enforced on the read path. `GET /{code}` for an expired code returns the\nexact same `404` body and headers as a code that never existed, so the redirect\nendpoint cannot be used as an enumeration oracle. Only\n`GET /api/links/{code}/stats` reveals expiry, via `200` with `\"expired\": true`.\n\n### Errors\n\nEvery error uses one envelope and never contains a stack trace, a database message\nor a filesystem path:\n\n```json\n{\"error\": {\"code\": \"not_found\", \"message\": \"No such link.\"}}\n```\n\n## Configuration\n\nAll configuration comes from environment variables.\n\n| Variable | Default | Purpose |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `LINKS_DB_PATH` | `./links.db` | Filesystem path to the SQLite database file (WAL mode). This is the single canonical name; `DATABASE_PATH` is never read. |\n| `LINKS_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8000` | Origin used to build the absolute `short_url` in the create response. Trailing slashes are stripped. |\n| `LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` | `true` | Master switch for all limiting. When false there is no per-IP bucket, no per-key bucket, no `429`, and `SHORTENER_API_KEYS` has no effect. |\n| `LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` | `10` | Maximum `POST /api/links` requests per window for the per-IP bucket. Applies only to callers without a recognised API key. |\n| `LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS` | `60` | Fixed-window length in seconds, shared by the per-IP bucket and every per-key bucket. Also the upper clamp for `Retry-After`. |\n| `LINKS_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR` | `false` | When true the per-IP identity is the leftmost `X-Forwarded-For` entry, otherwise the transport peer address. No influence on keyed callers. |\n| `SHORTENER_API_KEYS` | `\"\"` (empty) | Comma-separated `key:quota` pairs, e.g. `alpha:100,beta:20`, giving per-window `POST /api/links` quotas. Read once at startup. Unset or empty means no key is ever recognised. |\n\n### Secrets\n\nThis service **does** read one secret from the environment: `SHORTENER_API_KEYS`\ncontains API key material. (An earlier revision of this README claimed the service\nreads no secrets; that is no longer true.) Handling rules, enforced in code:\n\n* API keys are never written to SQLite, never logged, never placed in an exception\n message and never echoed in a response body \\* Limiter state is keyed by\n `blake2b(key, key=BOOT_SALT)` where `BOOT_SALT` is 32 random bytes generated once\n per process, so no plaintext key sits in an in-memory map.\n* Recognition is a constant-work hash plus a dict lookup, confirmed with\n `hmac.compare_digest`; there is no early-exit comparison loop over configured keys.\n* No key material is accepted at runtime through any admin route \\enforced entirely\n from the process environment.\n\n## Rate limiting\n\nLimiting runs as pure ASGI middleware in front of routing and body parsing, scoped\nto exactly `POST /api/links`, so a throttled request never opens a database\nconnection and never writes a row. `/health`, `/{code}` and the stats endpoint are\nnever refused with `429`.\n\n* **Recognised `X-API-Key`** (byte-exact, case-sensitive match against a configured\n key, surrounding whitespace stripped): only that key's bucket is consulted, using\n its configured quota. The per-IP bucket is neither read nor written, and the key's\n counter is shared across every client address.\n* **No key, empty/whitespace-only key, or unknown key**: the existing per-IP bucket\n and `LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` apply, exactly as before. Unknown keys allocate no\n per-key bucket, so random header values cannot grow memory or buy extra allowance.\n\nRefusals return `429` with `{\"error\": {\"code\": \"rate_limited\", ...}}`, an integer\n`Retry-After` header (at least 1, at most the window length) and `Cache-Control:\nno-store`.\n\nMalformed entries in `SHORTENER_API_KEYS` (`alpha` with no colon, `beta:abc`,\n`gamma:0`, `gamma:-5`, `:5`, empty segments) are ignored at startup; well formed\nentries in the same string still take effect. Whitespace around keys, quotas and\nseparators is stripped. If a key appears twice, the last occurrence wins.\n\nLimiter state is in-process and lost on restart.\n\n## URL safety\n\nTarget URLs are validated before they are stored, and the stored value is what is\nlater served in `Location`:\n\n* `http` and `https` only \\* every other scheme (`javascript:`, `data:`, `file:`, ...)\n is rejected by allow-list, not by blocking known bad names.\n* Embedded credentials (`https://user:pass@host/`) are rejected.\n* The host is resolved and every resulting address is rejected if it is loopback,\n private, link-local, multicast, reserved or unspecified. `169.254.169.254` (the\n cloud metadata endpoint) is denied explicitly.\n* Hosts that do not resolve are rejected.\n* Maximum length 2048 characters; control characters and whitespace are rejected.\n\nRedirect destinations only ever come from the validated, stored row \\* never from a\nquery parameter, header or path segment of the incoming request.\n\n## Running\n\n```bash\npip install -r requirements.txt\nuvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000\n```\n", "path": "README.md"}, {"content": "\"\"\"URL shortener service package.\n\nExposes the FastAPI application factory used by the ASGI server and the tests.\n\"\"\"\n\n__all__ = [\"__version__\"]\n\n__version__ = \"1.1.0\"\n", "path": "app/__init__.py"}, {"content": "\"\"\"Environment-driven configuration for the URL shortener service.\n\nAll settings come from environment variables with safe defaults. No secret is\nstored in this module: API key material is read separately (and never retained in\nplaintext) by :mod:`app.apikeys`.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport os\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Mapping, Optional\n\nLOGGER = logging.getLogger(\"shortener.config\")\n\nDEFAULT_DB_PATH: str = \"./links.db\"\nDEFAULT_BASE_URL: str = \"http://localhost:8000\"\nDEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED: bool = True\nDEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_MAX: int = 10\nDEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS: int = 60\nDEFAULT_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR: bool = False\n\nTRUE_VALUES = frozenset({\"1\", \"true\", \"yes\", \"on\"})\nFALSE_VALUES = frozenset({\"0\", \"false\", \"no\", \"off\"})\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Settings:\n \"\"\"Immutable snapshot of service configuration.\n\n Attributes:\n db_path: Filesystem path of the SQLite database file.\n base_url: Origin used to build absolute short URLs, without a trailing slash.\n rate_limit_enabled: Master switch for all rate limiting.\n rate_limit_max: Per-window allowance of the per-IP creation bucket.\n rate_limit_window_seconds: Fixed-window length shared by every bucket.\n trust_forwarded_for: Whether the leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry identifies\n the client for the per-IP bucket.\n \"\"\"\n\n db_path: str\n base_url: str\n rate_limit_enabled: bool\n rate_limit_max: int\n rate_limit_window_seconds: int\n trust_forwarded_for: bool\n\n\ndef _env_str(env: Mapping[str, str], name: str, default: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"Read a non-empty string environment variable.\n\n Args:\n env: Mapping to read from.\n name: Variable name.\n default: Value used when the variable is missing or blank.\n\n Returns:\n The stripped configured value, or ``default``.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n raw = env.get(name)\n if raw is None:\n return default\n value = raw.strip()\n return value if value else default\n\n\ndef _env_bool(env: Mapping[str, str], name: str, default: bool) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Read a boolean environment variable.\n\n Args:\n env: Mapping to read from.\n name: Variable name.\n default: Value used when the variable is missing, blank or unrecognised.\n\n Returns:\n The parsed boolean, or ``default`` when the value is not recognised.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n raw = env.get(name)\n if raw is None or not raw.strip():\n return default\n value = raw.strip().lower()\n if value in TRUE_VALUES:\n return True\n if value in FALSE_VALUES:\n return False\n LOGGER.warning(\"Unrecognised boolean for %s; using default %s\", name, default)\n return default\n\n\ndef _env_int(env: Mapping[str, str], name: str, default: int, minimum: int) -> int:\n \"\"\"Read a bounded integer environment variable.\n\n Args:\n env: Mapping to read from.\n name: Variable name.\n default: Value used when the variable is missing, blank, non-numeric or\n below ``minimum``.\n minimum: Smallest acceptable value.\n\n Returns:\n The parsed integer, or ``default``.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n raw = env.get(name)\n if raw is None or not raw.strip():\n return default\n try:\n value = int(raw.strip(), 10)\n except ValueError:\n LOGGER.warning(\"Non-integer value for %s; using default %d\", name, default)\n return default\n if value < minimum:\n LOGGER.warning(\"Value for %s below minimum %d; using default %d\", name, minimum, default)\n return default\n return value\n\n\ndef load_settings(env: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None) -> Settings:\n \"\"\"Build a :class:`Settings` instance from the environment.\n\n Args:\n env: Mapping to read from; defaults to ``os.environ``.\n\n Returns:\n A fully populated, immutable :class:`Settings`.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing: malformed values fall back to documented defaults.\n \"\"\"\n source: Mapping[str, str] = os.environ if env is None else env\n base_url = _env_str(source, \"LINKS_BASE_URL\", DEFAULT_BASE_URL).rstrip(\"/\")\n if not base_url:\n base_url = DEFAULT_BASE_URL\n return Settings(\n db_path=_env_str(source, \"LINKS_DB_PATH\", DEFAULT_DB_PATH),\n base_url=base_url,\n rate_limit_enabled=_env_bool(source, \"LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED\", DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED),\n rate_limit_max=_env_int(source, \"LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX\", DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_MAX, 1),\n rate_limit_window_seconds=_env_int(\n source, \"LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS\", DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS, 1\n ),\n trust_forwarded_for=_env_bool(source, \"LINKS_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR\", DEFAULT_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR),\n )\n", "path": "app/config.py"}, {"content": "\"\"\"Timezone-aware timestamp helpers.\n\nEvery timestamp handled by the service is timezone aware and stored as RFC 3339\nUTC text, so expiry comparisons cannot go wrong across a deployment boundary.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom typing import Optional\n\n\ndef utc_now() -> datetime:\n \"\"\"Return the current instant as a timezone-aware UTC datetime.\n\n Returns:\n The current time with ``tzinfo`` set to UTC.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n return datetime.now(timezone.utc)\n\n\ndef to_rfc3339(moment: datetime) -> str:\n \"\"\"Render a timezone-aware datetime as RFC 3339 UTC text.\n\n Args:\n moment: A timezone-aware datetime.\n\n Returns:\n The instant in UTC, e.g. ``2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z``.\n\n Raises:\n ValueError: If ``moment`` is naive (no tzinfo).\n \"\"\"\n if moment.tzinfo is None:\n raise ValueError(\"Refusing to serialise a naive datetime.\")\n return moment.astimezone(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace(\"+00:00\", \"Z\")\n\n\ndef parse_rfc3339(value: str) -> datetime:\n \"\"\"Parse RFC 3339 text into a timezone-aware UTC datetime.\n\n Args:\n value: Timestamp text, with or without a trailing ``Z``.\n\n Returns:\n The parsed instant, normalised to UTC.\n\n Raises:\n ValueError: If the text is not a parsable timestamp.\n \"\"\"\n text = value.strip()\n if text.endswith((\"Z\", \"z\")):\n text = text[:-1] + \"+00:00\"\n parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(text)\n if parsed.tzinfo is None:\n parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)\n return parsed.astimezone(timezone.utc)\n\n\ndef is_expired(expires_at: Optional[str], now: datetime) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Decide whether a stored expiry timestamp has passed.\n\n Args:\n expires_at: Stored RFC 3339 text, or ``None`` for a link that never expires.\n now: Timezone-aware reference instant.\n\n Returns:\n ``True`` when the link is expired (or its stored timestamp is unreadable,\n which is treated as expired so a corrupt row fails closed), ``False``\n otherwise.\n\n Raises:\n ValueError: If ``now`` is naive.\n \"\"\"\n if now.tzinfo is None:\n raise ValueError(\"Refusing to compare against a naive datetime.\")\n if expires_at is None:\n return False\n try:\n deadline = parse_rfc3339(expires_at)\n except ValueError:\n return True\n return deadline <= now\n", "path": "app/timeutil.py"}, {"content": "\"\"\"Stable JSON error envelope and the handlers that emit it.\n\nEvery error response has the shape ``{\"error\": {\"code\": ..., \"message\": ...}}`` and\nnever carries a stack trace, a database error string or a filesystem path.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nfrom typing import Dict, Mapping, Optional\n\nfrom fastapi import Request\nfrom fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError\nfrom fastapi.responses import JSONResponse\nfrom starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException\n\nLOGGER = logging.getLogger(\"shortener.errors\")\n\nSTATUS_ERROR_CODES: Dict[int, str] = {\n 400: \"bad_request\",\n 401: \"unauthorized\",\n 403: \"forbidden\",\n 404: \"not_found\",\n 405: \"method_not_allowed\",\n 409: \"conflict\",\n 413: \"payload_too_large\",\n 415: \"unsupported_media_type\",\n 422: \"validation_error\",\n 429: \"rate_limited\",\n 500: \"internal_error\",\n 503: \"service_unavailable\",\n}\n\n\ndef error_payload(code: str, message: str) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]:\n \"\"\"Build the canonical error envelope.\n\n Args:\n code: Stable machine-readable error code.\n message: Human-readable, non-sensitive description.\n\n Returns:\n The envelope dictionary ready to be serialised as JSON.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n return {\"error\": {\"code\": code, \"message\": message}}\n\n\nclass ApiError(StarletteHTTPException):\n \"\"\"HTTP exception carrying a stable error code for the JSON envelope.\"\"\"\n\n def __init__(\n self,\n status_code: int,\n error_code: str,\n message: str,\n headers: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None,\n ) -> None:\n \"\"\"Create an API error.\n\n Args:\n status_code: HTTP status to return.\n error_code: Stable code placed in ``error.code``.\n message: Safe message placed in ``error.message``.\n headers: Optional extra response headers.\n\n Returns:\n None.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n super().__init__(status_code=status_code, detail=message, headers=dict(headers or {}))\n self.error_code = error_code\n\n\nasync def api_error_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Render any HTTP exception through the shared error envelope.\n\n Args:\n request: The incoming request (unused beyond logging context).\n exc: The raised exception; expected to be an HTTPException subclass.\n\n Returns:\n A :class:`JSONResponse` carrying the error envelope.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if not isinstance(exc, StarletteHTTPException):\n return await unhandled_error_handler(request, exc)\n error_code = getattr(exc, \"error_code\", None) or STATUS_ERROR_CODES.get(exc.status_code, \"error\")\n detail = exc.detail if isinstance(exc.detail, str) and exc.detail else \"Request failed.\"\n return JSONResponse(\n status_code=exc.status_code,\n content=error_payload(str(error_code), detail),\n headers=dict(exc.headers or {}),\n )\n\n\nasync def validation_error_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Render request-model validation failures as a 422 envelope.\n\n Args:\n request: The incoming request (unused).\n exc: The raised :class:`RequestValidationError`.\n\n Returns:\n A 422 :class:`JSONResponse` with a generic, non-leaking message.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if isinstance(exc, RequestValidationError):\n LOGGER.info(\"Rejected invalid request body or parameters for %s\", request.url.path)\n return JSONResponse(\n status_code=422,\n content=error_payload(\"validation_error\", \"Request validation failed.\"),\n )\n\n\nasync def unhandled_error_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Render an unexpected exception as a 500 envelope without leaking details.\n\n Args:\n request: The incoming request, used only for a server-side log line.\n exc: The unhandled exception.\n\n Returns:\n A 500 :class:`JSONResponse` with a fixed message.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n LOGGER.exception(\"Unhandled error while serving %s %s\", request.method, request.url.path)\n return JSONResponse(\n status_code=500,\n content=error_payload(\"internal_error\", \"Internal server error.\"),\n )\n", "path": "app/errors.py"}, {"content": "\"\"\"Validation of user supplied target URLs.\n\nThe validated string is exactly what is stored, and the stored string is exactly\nwhat is later served in a ``Location`` header, so nothing that skipped validation\ncan ever be reached through the service.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport ipaddress\nimport socket\nfrom typing import FrozenSet, List, Set\nfrom urllib.parse import urlsplit\n\nMAX_URL_LENGTH: int = 2048\nALLOWED_SCHEMES: FrozenSet[str] = frozenset({\"http\", \"https\"})\nDEFAULT_PORTS = {\"http\": 80, \"https\": 443}\n\n# Cloud metadata endpoints: reaching these is how a URL handler leaks credentials.\nMETADATA_ADDRESSES: FrozenSet[str] = frozenset({\"169.254.169.254\", \"fd00:ec2::254\"})\n\n\nclass UrlValidationError(ValueError):\n \"\"\"Raised when a target URL is not safe to store or serve.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _has_forbidden_characters(raw: str) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Report whether a URL contains control characters or whitespace.\n\n Args:\n raw: Candidate URL text.\n\n Returns:\n ``True`` when the text contains whitespace or C0/C1 control characters.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n for char in raw:\n code_point = ord(char)\n if char.isspace() or code_point < 0x20 or code_point == 0x7F:\n return True\n return False\n\n\ndef is_blocked_address(address: str) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Decide whether a resolved IP address must not be reachable via a short link.\n\n Args:\n address: Textual IPv4 or IPv6 address.\n\n Returns:\n ``True`` when the address is loopback, private, link-local, multicast,\n reserved, unspecified, a known metadata endpoint, or unparsable.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n try:\n parsed = ipaddress.ip_address(address)\n except ValueError:\n return True\n if isinstance(parsed, ipaddress.IPv6Address) and parsed.ipv4_mapped is not None:\n parsed = parsed.ipv4_mapped\n if str(parsed) in METADATA_ADDRESSES:\n return True\n if parsed.is_loopback or parsed.is_private or parsed.is_link_local:\n return True\n if parsed.is_multicast or parsed.is_reserved or parsed.is_unspecified:\n return True\n if getattr(parsed, \"is_site_local\", False):\n return True\n return False\n\n\ndef _resolve_host(host: str, port: int) -> List[str]:\n \"\"\"Resolve a hostname (or IP literal) to every address it maps to.\n\n Args:\n host: Hostname or IP literal taken from the URL.\n port: Port used for the lookup.\n\n Returns:\n A list of textual addresses, never empty.\n\n Raises:\n UrlValidationError: If the host cannot be resolved.\n \"\"\"\n try:\n infos = socket.getaddrinfo(host, port, proto=socket.IPPROTO_TCP)\n except (socket.gaierror, UnicodeError, OSError) as exc:\n raise UrlValidationError(\"Target host could not be resolved.\") from exc\n addresses: Set[str] = set()\n for info in infos:\n sockaddr = info[4]\n if sockaddr and isinstance(sockaddr[0], str):\n addresses.add(sockaddr[0])\n if not addresses:\n raise UrlValidationError(\"Target host could not be resolved.\")\n return sorted(addresses)\n\n\ndef validate_target_url(raw: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"Validate a user supplied target URL and return the value to store.\n\n The URL must use http or https (allow-list, so ``javascript:``, ``data:``,\n ``file:`` and every other scheme are refused), must not embed credentials, and\n must resolve exclusively to publicly routable addresses.\n\n Args:\n raw: The candidate URL exactly as supplied by the client.\n\n Returns:\n The URL string to persist, byte-identical to the accepted input.\n\n Raises:\n UrlValidationError: If the URL is malformed, too long, uses a disallowed\n scheme, embeds credentials, or resolves to a blocked address.\n \"\"\"\n if not raw:\n raise UrlValidationError(\"URL must not be empty.\")\n if len(raw) > MAX_URL_LENGTH:\n raise UrlValidationError(\"URL exceeds the maximum length of 2048 characters.\")\n if _has_forbidden_characters(raw):\n raise UrlValidationError(\"URL must not contain whitespace or control characters.\")\n\n try:\n parts = urlsplit(raw)\n except ValueError as exc:\n raise UrlValidationError(\"URL could not be parsed.\") from exc\n\n scheme = parts.scheme.lower()\n if scheme not in ALLOWED_SCHEMES:\n raise UrlValidationError(\"URL scheme must be http or https.\")\n if parts.username is not None or parts.password is not None or \"@\" in parts.netloc:\n raise UrlValidationError(\"URL must not contain embedded credentials.\")\n\n try:\n hostname = parts.hostname\n port = parts.port\n except ValueError as exc:\n raise UrlValidationError(\"URL contains an invalid port.\") from exc\n if not hostname:\n raise UrlValidationError(\"URL must contain a host.\")\n if port is not None and not (1 <= port <= 65535):\n raise UrlValidationError(\"URL contains an invalid port.\")\n\n lookup_port = port if port is not None else DEFAULT_PORTS[scheme]\n for address in _resolve_host(hostname, lookup_port):\n if is_blocked_address(address):\n raise UrlValidationError(\"URL resolves to a network address that is not allowed.\")\n return raw\n", "path": "app/urlvalidation.py"}, {"content": "\"\"\"Per-key POST quotas parsed from SHORTENER_API_KEYS.\n\nKey material is a secret. It is hashed with a per-boot salt on the way in and the\nplaintext is never retained as a dict key, attribute, log field or exception\nargument, never written to SQLite and never placed in a response body.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hashlib\nimport hmac\nimport logging\nimport secrets\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Dict, Mapping, Optional\n\nLOGGER = logging.getLogger(\"shortener.apikeys\")\n\n#: 32 random bytes, generated once per process, never logged or serialised.\nBOOT_SALT: bytes = secrets.token_bytes(32)\n\n#: Longest header value considered as a possible key; anything longer is unknown.\nMAX_KEY_LENGTH: int = 512\n\n\ndef salted_digest(material: bytes) -> bytes:\n \"\"\"Hash arbitrary identity material with the per-boot salt.\n\n Args:\n material: Raw bytes (an API key or a client address) to hash.\n\n Returns:\n A 32-byte digest that is stable within this process only.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n return hashlib.blake2b(material, key=BOOT_SALT, digest_size=32).digest()\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ApiKeyEntry:\n \"\"\"A recognised API key, represented only by its salted digest and quota.\n\n Attributes:\n digest: Salted hash of the configured key.\n quota: Allowed POST /api/links requests per window; always >= 1.\n \"\"\"\n\n digest: bytes\n quota: int\n\n\ndef parse_api_key_quotas(raw: Optional[str]) -> Dict[bytes, ApiKeyEntry]:\n \"\"\"Parse the SHORTENER_API_KEYS value into a digest-keyed quota table.\n\n The value is a comma-separated list of ``key:quota`` pairs. Whitespace around\n keys, quotas and separators is stripped. Entries without a colon, with a blank\n key, or with a non-integer / zero / negative quota are dropped. When a key\n appears more than once the last occurrence wins.\n\n Args:\n raw: The raw environment value, possibly ``None`` or empty.\n\n Returns:\n A mapping of salted digest to :class:`ApiKeyEntry`. Empty when nothing is\n configured, in which case no key is ever recognised.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing: malformed entries are ignored so the service always starts.\n \"\"\"\n table: Dict[bytes, ApiKeyEntry] = {}\n dropped = 0\n for segment in (raw or \"\").split(\",\"):\n item = segment.strip()\n if not item:\n continue\n key_part, separator, quota_part = item.partition(\":\")\n if not separator:\n dropped += 1\n continue\n key = key_part.strip()\n quota_text = quota_part.strip()\n if not key or not quota_text or len(key) > MAX_KEY_LENGTH:\n dropped += 1\n continue\n try:\n quota = int(quota_text, 10)\n except ValueError:\n dropped += 1\n continue\n if quota < 1:\n dropped += 1\n continue\n digest = salted_digest(key.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n table[digest] = ApiKeyEntry(digest=digest, quota=quota)\n if dropped:\n LOGGER.warning(\"Ignored %d malformed SHORTENER_API_KEYS entries.\", dropped)\n LOGGER.info(\"Loaded %d API key quota entries.\", len(table))\n return table\n\n\ndef lookup_api_key(\n table: Mapping[bytes, ApiKeyEntry], presented: Optional[str]\n) -> Optional[ApiKeyEntry]:\n \"\"\"Look up the quota for a presented API key.\n\n Recognition is one constant-work hash plus a hash-table lookup, confirmed with\n :func:`hmac.compare_digest`, so there is no early-exit comparison loop over the\n configured key set to time. Matching is byte-exact and case-sensitive; a header\n that is absent, empty or whitespace-only counts as no key at all.\n\n Args:\n table: The digest-keyed quota table built at startup.\n presented: The raw ``X-API-Key`` header value, if any.\n\n Returns:\n The matching :class:`ApiKeyEntry`, or ``None`` when the caller presented no\n key or an unrecognised one.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if not table or presented is None:\n return None\n candidate = presented.strip()\n if not candidate or len(candidate) > MAX_KEY_LENGTH:\n return None\n digest = salted_digest(candidate.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n entry = table.get(digest)\n if entry is None:\n return None\n if not hmac.compare_digest(digest, entry.digest):\n return None\n return entry\n", "path": "app/apikeys.py"}, {"content": "\"\"\"Fixed-window rate limiting for POST /api/links.\n\nEnforcement lives in one place: a pure ASGI middleware that runs before routing and\nbefore body parsing, scoped to exactly ``POST /api/links``. A throttled request\ntherefore never opens a database connection and never writes a row, and no other\nroute (``/health``, ``/{code}``, the stats endpoint) can ever be refused with 429.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport math\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom typing import Callable, Dict, Mapping, NamedTuple, Optional, Tuple\n\nfrom starlette.types import ASGIApp, Receive, Scope, Send\n\nfrom .apikeys import ApiKeyEntry, lookup_api_key, salted_digest\n\n#: Upper bound on entries tracked in each bucket map, applied independently.\nMAX_TRACKED_KEYS: int = 10000\n\n#: The only path the limiter guards.\nCREATE_LINK_PATH: str = \"/api/links\"\n\nRATE_LIMITED_BODY: bytes = json.dumps(\n {\"error\": {\"code\": \"rate_limited\", \"message\": \"Rate limit exceeded. Please retry later.\"}},\n separators=(\",\", \":\"),\n).encode(\"utf-8\")\n\n\nclass RateLimitDecision(NamedTuple):\n \"\"\"Outcome of a limiter consultation.\n\n Attributes:\n allowed: Whether the request may proceed.\n retry_after: Whole seconds to wait; meaningful only when refused.\n \"\"\"\n\n allowed: bool\n retry_after: int\n\n\nclass RateLimiter:\n \"\"\"In-process fixed-window counters for unkeyed and keyed link creation.\n\n Two namespaces are kept: ``ip_buckets`` for callers without a recognised API key\n and ``key_buckets`` for callers presenting one. A recognised key substitutes for\n the per-IP bucket rather than adding to it, so a configured quota means exactly\n what the operator wrote. State is lost on restart.\n \"\"\"\n\n def __init__(\n self,\n *,\n enabled: bool,\n max_requests: int,\n window_seconds: int,\n trust_forwarded_for: bool,\n api_key_quotas: Mapping[bytes, ApiKeyEntry],\n ) -> None:\n \"\"\"Create a limiter.\n\n Args:\n enabled: Master switch; when false nothing is counted or refused.\n max_requests: Per-window allowance of the per-IP bucket.\n window_seconds: Fixed-window length, shared by all buckets.\n trust_forwarded_for: Whether to use the leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry\n as the per-IP identity.\n api_key_quotas: Digest-keyed quota table built at startup.\n\n Returns:\n None.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n self.enabled: bool = bool(enabled)\n self.max_requests: int = max(1, int(max_requests))\n self.window_seconds: int = max(1, int(window_seconds))\n self.trust_forwarded_for: bool = bool(trust_forwarded_for)\n self.api_key_quotas: Dict[bytes, ApiKeyEntry] = dict(api_key_quotas)\n self.ip_buckets: Dict[bytes, Tuple[float, int]] = {}\n self.key_buckets: Dict[bytes, Tuple[float, int]] = {}\n self.clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic\n self.lock = threading.Lock()\n\n def reset(self) -> None:\n \"\"\"Discard all counters.\n\n Returns:\n None.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n with self.lock:\n self.ip_buckets.clear()\n self.key_buckets.clear()\n\n def _prune_locked(self, buckets: Dict[bytes, Tuple[float, int]], now: float) -> None:\n \"\"\"Bound a bucket map, dropping stale then oldest entries.\n\n Must be called with :attr:`lock` held.\n\n Args:\n buckets: The map to prune in place.\n now: Current clock reading.\n\n Returns:\n None.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if len(buckets) <= MAX_TRACKED_KEYS:\n return\n stale = [key for key, (started, _) in buckets.items() if now - started >= self.window_seconds]\n for key in stale:\n del buckets[key]\n overflow = len(buckets) - MAX_TRACKED_KEYS\n if overflow <= 0:\n return\n oldest = sorted(buckets.items(), key=lambda item: item[1][0])[:overflow]\n for key, _ in oldest:\n del buckets[key]\n\n def _consume(\n self, buckets: Dict[bytes, Tuple[float, int]], identity: bytes, quota: int\n ) -> RateLimitDecision:\n \"\"\"Count one request against a bucket and decide whether to allow it.\n\n Args:\n buckets: The namespace to charge (per-IP or per-key).\n identity: Salted digest identifying the caller within that namespace.\n quota: Requests permitted per window for this identity.\n\n Returns:\n A :class:`RateLimitDecision`.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n with self.lock:\n now = self.clock()\n started, count = buckets.get(identity, (now, 0))\n if now - started >= self.window_seconds:\n started, count = now, 0\n if count >= quota:\n remaining = (started + self.window_seconds) - now\n retry_after = int(math.ceil(remaining)) if remaining > 0 else 1\n retry_after = max(1, min(self.window_seconds, retry_after))\n buckets[identity] = (started, count)\n return RateLimitDecision(allowed=False, retry_after=retry_after)\n buckets[identity] = (started, count + 1)\n self._prune_locked(buckets, now)\n return RateLimitDecision(allowed=True, retry_after=0)\n\n def check_create(self, api_key: Optional[str], client_address: str) -> RateLimitDecision:\n \"\"\"Consult the limiter for one POST /api/links request.\n\n A recognised API key is charged to its own bucket using its own quota and\n the per-IP bucket is neither read nor written. No key, a blank key or an\n unrecognised key falls through to the per-IP bucket and allocates nothing\n keyed by the header value.\n\n Args:\n api_key: Raw ``X-API-Key`` header value, if present.\n client_address: Client identity for the per-IP bucket.\n\n Returns:\n A :class:`RateLimitDecision`; always allowed when limiting is disabled.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if not self.enabled:\n return RateLimitDecision(allowed=True, retry_after=0)\n entry = lookup_api_key(self.api_key_quotas, api_key)\n if entry is not None:\n return self._consume(self.key_buckets, entry.digest, entry.quota)\n identity = salted_digest(client_address.encode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\"))\n return self._consume(self.ip_buckets, identity, self.max_requests)\n\n\ndef header_value(scope: Scope, name: bytes) -> Optional[str]:\n \"\"\"Read a single request header from an ASGI scope.\n\n Args:\n scope: The ASGI HTTP scope.\n name: Lower-case header name as bytes.\n\n Returns:\n The decoded header value, or ``None`` when absent or undecodable.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n for raw_name, raw_value in scope.get(\"headers\", []):\n if raw_name == name:\n try:\n return raw_value.decode(\"utf-8\")\n except UnicodeDecodeError:\n return None\n return None\n\n\ndef client_address(scope: Scope, trust_forwarded_for: bool) -> str:\n \"\"\"Determine the per-IP bucket identity for a request.\n\n Args:\n scope: The ASGI HTTP scope.\n trust_forwarded_for: Whether to honour ``X-Forwarded-For``.\n\n Returns:\n The client address text, or ``\"unknown\"`` when it cannot be determined.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if trust_forwarded_for:\n forwarded = header_value(scope, b\"x-forwarded-for\")\n if forwarded:\n first = forwarded.split(\",\")[0].strip()\n if first:\n return first[:255]\n client = scope.get(\"client\")\n if client and isinstance(client, (tuple, list)) and client[0]:\n return str(client[0])[:255]\n return \"unknown\"\n\n\ndef _normalised_path(scope: Scope) -> str:\n \"\"\"Return the request path without root prefix or trailing slash.\n\n Args:\n scope: The ASGI HTTP scope.\n\n Returns:\n The normalised path, always beginning with ``/``.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n path = scope.get(\"path\") or \"/\"\n root_path = scope.get(\"root_path\") or \"\"\n if root_path and path.startswith(root_path):\n path = path[len(root_path) :] or \"/\"\n if len(path) > 1:\n path = path.rstrip(\"/\") or \"/\"\n return path\n\n\nclass RateLimitMiddleware:\n \"\"\"ASGI middleware applying :class:`RateLimiter` to link creation only.\"\"\"\n\n def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp, limiter: RateLimiter) -> None:\n \"\"\"Wrap an ASGI application.\n\n Args:\n app: The next application in the stack.\n limiter: Shared limiter instance (also exposed on ``app.state``).\n\n Returns:\n None.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n self.app = app\n self.limiter = limiter\n\n def _guards(self, scope: Scope) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Report whether this request is subject to limiting.\n\n Args:\n scope: The ASGI HTTP scope.\n\n Returns:\n ``True`` only for ``POST /api/links``.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n method = str(scope.get(\"method\", \"\")).upper()\n return method == \"POST\" and _normalised_path(scope) == CREATE_LINK_PATH\n\n async def _send_rate_limited(self, send: Send, retry_after: int) -> None:\n \"\"\"Emit the 429 refusal response.\n\n Args:\n send: The ASGI send callable.\n retry_after: Whole seconds for the ``Retry-After`` header.\n\n Returns:\n None.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n headers = [\n (b\"content-type\", b\"application/json\"),\n (b\"content-length\", str(len(RATE_LIMITED_BODY)).encode(\"ascii\")),\n (b\"retry-after\", str(retry_after).encode(\"ascii\")),\n (b\"cache-control\", b\"no-store\"),\n ]\n await send({\"type\": \"http.response.start\", \"status\": 429, \"headers\": headers})\n await send({\"type\": \"http.response.body\", \"body\": RATE_LIMITED_BODY, \"more_body\": False})\n\n async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:\n \"\"\"Handle one ASGI event stream.\n\n Args:\n scope: The ASGI scope.\n receive: The ASGI receive callable.\n send: The ASGI send callable.\n\n Returns:\n None.\n\n Raises:\n Exception: Anything raised by the wrapped application.\n \"\"\"\n if scope.get(\"type\") != \"http\" or not self._guards(scope):\n await self.app(scope, receive, send)\n return\n decision = self.limiter.check_create(\n header_value(scope, b\"x-api-key\"),\n client_address(scope, self.limiter.trust_forwarded_for),\n )\n if decision.allowed:\n await self.app(scope, receive, send)\n return\n await self._send_rate_limited(send, decision.retry_after)\n", "path": "app/ratelimit.py"}, {"content": "\"\"\"SQLite access layer.\n\nEvery statement is parameterised; no SQL is ever built with string formatting.\nSchema is created if missing and is otherwise untouched.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport os\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import closing\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom typing import Optional, Tuple\n\nfrom .timeutil import is_expired, to_rfc3339\n\nLOGGER = logging.getLogger(\"shortener.db\")\n\nSCHEMA_STATEMENTS = (\n \"\"\"\n CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (\n id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n target_url TEXT NOT NULL,\n created_at TEXT NOT NULL,\n expires_at TEXT\n )\n \"\"\",\n \"\"\"\n CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clicks (\n id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n code TEXT NOT NULL,\n clicked_at TEXT NOT NULL\n )\n \"\"\",\n \"CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_clicks_code ON clicks(code)\",\n)\n\n\ndef connect(db_path: str) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n \"\"\"Open a SQLite connection in autocommit mode.\n\n Args:\n db_path: Filesystem path of the database file.\n\n Returns:\n A connection with ``sqlite3.Row`` rows and manual transaction control.\n\n Raises:\n sqlite3.Error: If the database cannot be opened.\n \"\"\"\n conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=10.0, isolation_level=None)\n conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n return conn\n\n\ndef init_db(db_path: str) -> None:\n \"\"\"Create the database file, directory and schema when they are missing.\n\n Args:\n db_path: Filesystem path of the database file.\n\n Returns:\n None.\n\n Raises:\n sqlite3.Error: If the schema cannot be created.\n OSError: If the containing directory cannot be created.\n \"\"\"\n directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(db_path))\n if directory:\n os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)\n with closing(connect(db_path)) as conn:\n conn.execute(\"PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL\")\n conn.execute(\"PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL\")\n for statement in SCHEMA_STATEMENTS:\n conn.execute(statement)\n LOGGER.info(\"Database ready.\")\n\n\ndef insert_link(\n conn: sqlite3.Connection,\n code: str,\n target_url: str,\n created_at: datetime,\n expires_at: Optional[datetime],\n) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Insert one link row.\n\n Args:\n conn: Open connection.\n code: Short code, unique across the table.\n target_url: Already validated destination URL.\n created_at: Timezone-aware creation instant.\n expires_at: Timezone-aware expiry instant, or ``None`` for never.\n\n Returns:\n ``True`` when the row was written, ``False`` when the code was already taken.\n\n Raises:\n sqlite3.Error: On any database failure other than the uniqueness conflict.\n ValueError: If a naive datetime is supplied.\n \"\"\"\n try:\n conn.execute(\n \"INSERT INTO links (code, target_url, created_at, expires_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n (\n code,\n target_url,\n to_rfc3339(created_at),\n to_rfc3339(expires_at) if expires_at is not None else None,\n ),\n )\n except sqlite3.IntegrityError:\n return False\n return True\n\n\ndef get_link(conn: sqlite3.Connection, code: str) -> Optional[sqlite3.Row]:\n \"\"\"Fetch one link row by code.\n\n Args:\n conn: Open connection.\n code: Short code to look up.\n\n Returns:\n The row with ``target_url``, ``created_at`` and ``expires_at``, or ``None``.\n\n Raises:\n sqlite3.Error: On any database failure.\n \"\"\"\n cursor = conn.execute(\n \"SELECT code, target_url, created_at, expires_at FROM links WHERE code = ?\",\n (code,),\n )\n return cursor.fetchone()\n\n\ndef get_click_stats(conn: sqlite3.Connection, code: str) -> Tuple[int, Optional[str]]:\n \"\"\"Summarise recorded clicks for one code.\n\n Args:\n conn: Open connection.\n code: Short code to summarise.\n\n Returns:\n A tuple of (click count, last click timestamp or ``None``).\n\n Raises:\n sqlite3.Error: On any database failure.\n \"\"\"\n row = conn.execute(\n \"SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, MAX(clicked_at) AS last_clicked_at FROM clicks WHERE code = ?\",\n (code,),\n ).fetchone()\n if row is None:\n return 0, None\n last = row[\"last_clicked_at\"]\n return int(row[\"total\"] or 0), str(last) if last is not None else None\n\n\ndef resolve_redirect(conn: sqlite3.Connection, code: str, now: datetime) -> Optional[str]:\n \"\"\"Look up a live target URL and record the click in the same transaction.\n\n Args:\n conn: Open connection.\n code: Short code requested by the visitor.\n now: Timezone-aware instant of the request.\n\n Returns:\n The stored target URL when the link exists and has not expired, otherwise\n ``None`` (no click is recorded in that case).\n\n Raises:\n sqlite3.Error: On any database failure.\n ValueError: If ``now`` is naive.\n \"\"\"\n conn.execute(\"BEGIN IMMEDIATE\")\n try:\n row = conn.execute(\n \"SELECT target_url, expires_at FROM links WHERE code = ?\",\n (code,),\n ).fetchone()\n if row is None or is_expired(row[\"expires_at\"], now):\n conn.rollback()\n return None\n conn.execute(\n \"INSERT INTO clicks (code, clicked_at) VALUES (?, ?)\",\n (code, to_rfc3339(now)),\n )\n conn.commit()\n return str(row[\"target_url\"])\n except Exception:\n conn.rollback()\n raise\n", "path": "app/db.py"}, {"content": "\"\"\"Typed request and response models used at the HTTP boundary.\n\nEvery string that reaches the database has an explicit length limit here, and the\nmodels are strict: values of the wrong type are rejected rather than coerced.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom pydantic import AliasChoices, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field\n\nMAX_URL_LENGTH: int = 2048\nMAX_CODE_LENGTH: int = 32\nMIN_CODE_LENGTH: int = 3\nCODE_PATTERN: str = r\"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$\"\nMAX_TTL_SECONDS: int = 31_536_000 # one year\n\n\nclass CreateLinkRequest(BaseModel):\n \"\"\"Body of ``POST /api/links``.\n\n Attributes:\n url: Destination URL; validated for scheme, credentials and address safety\n before it is stored.\n expires_in_seconds: Optional lifetime in seconds; omit for a link that never\n expires.\n code: Optional custom short code.\n \"\"\"\n\n model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True, populate_by_name=True, extra=\"ignore\")\n\n url: str = Field(\n ...,\n min_length=1,\n max_length=MAX_URL_LENGTH,\n validation_alias=AliasChoices(\"url\", \"target_url\", \"long_url\"),\n description=\"Destination URL (http or https only).\",\n )\n expires_in_seconds: Optional[int] = Field(\n default=None,\n ge=1,\n le=MAX_TTL_SECONDS,\n validation_alias=AliasChoices(\"expires_in_seconds\", \"expires_in\", \"ttl_seconds\"),\n description=\"Lifetime in seconds; omitted means the link never expires.\",\n )\n code: Optional[str] = Field(\n default=None,\n min_length=MIN_CODE_LENGTH,\n max_length=MAX_CODE_LENGTH,\n pattern=CODE_PATTERN,\n validation_alias=AliasChoices(\"code\", \"custom_code\", \"alias\"),\n description=\"Optional custom short code.\",\n )\n\n\nclass LinkCreatedResponse(BaseModel):\n \"\"\"Body of a successful ``POST /api/links``.\n\n Attributes:\n code: The allocated short code.\n short_url: Absolute short URL built from LINKS_BASE_URL.\n target_url: The stored, validated destination.\n created_at: RFC 3339 UTC creation timestamp.\n expires_at: RFC 3339 UTC expiry timestamp, or ``None``.\n \"\"\"\n\n code: str\n short_url: str\n target_url: str\n created_at: str\n expires_at: Optional[str] = None\n\n\nclass LinkStatsResponse(BaseModel):\n \"\"\"Body of ``GET /api/links/{code}/stats``.\n\n Attributes:\n code: The short code.\n target_url: The stored destination.\n created_at: RFC 3339 UTC creation timestamp.\n expires_at: RFC 3339 UTC expiry timestamp, or ``None``.\n expired: Whether the link has passed its expiry instant.\n click_count: Number of redirects served for this code.\n last_clicked_at: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of the most recent click, if any.\n \"\"\"\n\n code: str\n target_url: str\n created_at: str\n expires_at: Optional[str] = None\n expired: bool\n click_count: int\n last_clicked_at: Optional[str] = None\n\n\nclass HealthResponse(BaseModel):\n \"\"\"Body of ``GET /health``.\n\n Attributes:\n status: Always ``\"ok\"`` when the process is serving requests.\n \"\"\"\n\n status: str\n", "path": "app/schemas.py"}, {"content": "\"\"\"HTTP routes for the URL shortener.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport secrets\nfrom contextlib import closing\nfrom datetime import timedelta\nfrom typing import FrozenSet, Optional\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Request, status\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom .config import Settings\nfrom .db import connect, get_click_stats, get_link, insert_link, resolve_redirect\nfrom .errors import ApiError\nfrom .schemas import (\n CreateLinkRequest,\n HealthResponse,\n LinkCreatedResponse,\n LinkStatsResponse,\n)\nfrom .timeutil import is_expired, to_rfc3339, utc_now\nfrom .urlvalidation import UrlValidationError, validate_target_url\n\nLOGGER = logging.getLogger(\"shortener.routes\")\n\nrouter = APIRouter()\n\nCODE_ALPHABET: str = \"abcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789\"\nCODE_LENGTH: int = 7\nMAX_CODE_ATTEMPTS: int = 10\nMAX_PATH_CODE_LENGTH: int = 64\nALLOWED_CODE_CHARS: FrozenSet[str] = frozenset(\n \"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-\"\n)\nRESERVED_CODES: FrozenSet[str] = frozenset(\n {\"health\", \"api\", \"docs\", \"redoc\", \"openapi.json\", \"favicon.ico\", \"static\", \"metrics\"}\n)\nNOT_FOUND_MESSAGE: str = \"No such link.\"\n\n\ndef _settings(request: Request) -> Settings:\n \"\"\"Fetch the configuration snapshot attached to the application.\n\n Args:\n request: The incoming request.\n\n Returns:\n The :class:`Settings` stored on ``app.state``.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n settings: Settings = request.app.state.settings\n return settings\n\n\ndef _is_valid_code(code: str) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Report whether a path segment could be a short code.\n\n Args:\n code: Candidate short code taken from the URL path.\n\n Returns:\n ``True`` when the code has a plausible length and character set.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if not code or len(code) > MAX_PATH_CODE_LENGTH:\n return False\n return all(char in ALLOWED_CODE_CHARS for char in code)\n\n\ndef _generate_code() -> str:\n \"\"\"Generate a random, unpredictable short code.\n\n Returns:\n A 7-character code drawn from an unambiguous alphabet.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n return \"\".join(secrets.choice(CODE_ALPHABET) for _ in range(CODE_LENGTH))\n\n\n@router.get(\n \"/health\",\n response_model=HealthResponse,\n status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,\n tags=[\"ops\"],\n summary=\"Liveness probe\",\n)\ndef health() -> HealthResponse:\n \"\"\"Report process liveness without reading user data.\n\n Returns:\n A :class:`HealthResponse` with status ``\"ok\"``.\n\n Raises:\n Nothing.\n \"\"\"\n return HealthResponse(status=\"ok\")\n\n\n@router.post(\n \"/api/links\",\n response_model=LinkCreatedResponse,\n status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,\n tags=[\"links\"],\n summary=\"Create a short link\",\n)\ndef create_link(payload: CreateLinkRequest, request: Request) -> LinkCreatedResponse:\n \"\"\"Validate a target URL and store a new short link.\n\n Args:\n payload: Validated request body.\n request: The incoming request, used for configuration access.\n\n Returns:\n A :class:`LinkCreatedResponse` describing the stored link.\n\n Raises:\n ApiError: 422 when the URL is unsafe or malformed, 409 when a requested\n custom code is unavailable, 500 when no free code could be allocated.\n \"\"\"\n settings = _settings(request)\n try:\n target_url = validate_target_url(payload.url)\n except UrlValidationError as exc:\n raise ApiError(422, \"validation_error\", str(exc)) from exc\n\n created_at = utc_now()\n expires_at = (\n created_at + timedelta(seconds=payload.expires_in_seconds)\n if payload.expires_in_seconds is not None\n else None\n )\n\n with closing(connect(settings.db_path)) as conn:\n if payload.code is not None:\n if payload.code.lower() in RESERVED_CODES:\n raise ApiError(409, \"code_unavailable\", \"Short code is not available.\")\n if not insert_link(conn, payload.code, target_url, created_at, expires_at):\n raise ApiError(409, \"code_unavailable\", \"Short code is not available.\")\n code = payload.code\n else:\n code = \"\"\n for _ in range(MAX_CODE_ATTEMPTS):\n candidate = _generate_code()\n if insert_link(conn, candidate, target_url, created_at, expires_at):\n code = candidate\n break\n if not code:\n raise ApiError(500, \"internal_error\", \"Could not allocate a short code.\")\n\n return LinkCreatedResponse(\n code=code,\n short_url=settings.base_url + \"/\" + code,\n The generic house rule says limit creation AND redirects; the design's enforcement decision and several acceptance criteria say the opposite explicitly (\"/health, /{code} and the stats endpoint can never be refused with 429\", \"a keyed caller whose quota is spent can still follow links\"). I followed the design: the middleware is scoped to exactly POST /api/links. Adding a redirect bucket would have made those criteria and the existing suite fail.\n\n2. Request body shape. The portion of the design describing the POST /api/links request/response schema was truncated in my copy, so I chose: {\"url\": str, \"expires_in_seconds\": int|null, \"code\": str|null} with validation aliases (url|target_url|long_url, expires_in_seconds|expires_in|ttl_seconds, code|custom_code|alias) and pydantic strict=True (no type coercion), extra=\"ignore\" so an unexpected extra field does not 422. Length limits: url <= 2048, code 3-32 matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]. Response is {code, short_url, target_url, created_at, expires_at} with 201.\n\n3. Unresolvable hosts are rejected (422 validation_error). This is the safe option and is required by the SSRF rule, but it means link creation needs working DNS for the target host in the test environment.\n\n4. Presented X-API-Key values are .strip()ed before hashing, matching the stripping applied to configured keys; matching is otherwise byte-exact and case-sensitive. Empty/whitespace-only headers are treated as absent. Header values longer than 512 bytes or not UTF-8 decodable are treated as unknown (fall back to the per-IP bucket, no allocation).\n\n5. SHORTENER_API_KEYS parsing splits each segment on the FIRST colon, so \"alpha:5:6\" is malformed and dropped rather than silently becoming key \"alpha:5\". Last occurrence of a key wins; quota must parse as an integer >= 1.\n\n6. Config parsing: values that are blank, non-numeric or below the documented minimum fall back to the documented default (with a warning log); rate_limit_max and window are clamped to >= 1 so a misconfiguration cannot produce a zero-length window or a Retry-After of 0.\n\n7. Retry-After = ceil(window_start + window - now), clamped to [1, LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS]. The 429 body is a fixed pre-serialised envelope with Cache-Control: no-store, emitted directly by the ASGI middleware, so no DB connection is opened and no key material can leak into it.\n\n8. SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:100,beta:20\", LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10, 100 consecutive POST /api/links requests carrying header X-API-Key: alpha within one window all integer >= 1 and <= 60, Cache-Control: no-store, and leaves the links table row count unchanged (no row written for the refused request).\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:100,beta:20\", 20 creations with X-API-Key: beta return 201 and the 21st returns 429, proving the quota is read per key and not shared.\n- After key alpha has been throttled to 429, the next POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: beta returns 201, proving quotas are independent per key.\n- With LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10 and quota alpha:100, 11 consecutive keyed creations from one client address all return 201, proving a known key is limited by its quota only and not additionally by the per-IP bucket.\n- With LINKS_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR=true and quota alpha:3, three creations sent from X-Forwarded-For 203.0.113.10 with key gamma (not present in SHORTENER_API_KEYS) is counted in the same per-IP bucket as a request with no key at all: 10 mixed keyed-unknown and unkeyed creations from one address succeed and the 11th returns 429.\n- Key matching is exact and case-sensitive: with alpha configured, X-API-Key: ALPHA is treated as unknown and falls back to the per-IP limit.\n- An X-API-Key header present but empty, or whitespace only, is treated as no key and falls back to the per-IP limit.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS unset or set to an empty string, every request behaves exactly as today; the X-API-Key header has no effect on any response.\n- Malformed entries in SHORTENER_API_KEYS (\"alpha\" with no colon, \"beta:abc\", \"gamma:0\", \"gamma:-5\", \":5\", empty segments) are ignored at startup while any well formed entry in the same string still takes effect; the service starts and serves requests normally.\n- SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\" alpha : 100 , beta:20 \" yields working quotas of 100 for alpha and 20 for beta (surrounding whitespace around keys, quotas and separators is stripped).\n- When the same key appears twice, e.g. \"alpha:5,alpha:9\", the last occurrence wins and the effective quota is 9.\n- After the 60 second window has elapsed (simulated by advancing the limiter's clock, not by sleeping), a previously throttled key's next creation returns 201.\n- GET /{code} redirects return 307 regardless of the X-API-Key header and regardless of whether that key's creation quota is exhausted; a keyed caller whose quota is spent can still follow links.\n- GET /api/links/{code}/stats and GET /health are never refused with 429 on account of any API key quota.\n- With LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false, 15 consecutive creations carrying X-API-Key: beta (quota 20) and 15 carrying no key all return 201; no limiting of any kind occurs.\n- No schema change: after exercising keyed and unkeyed creation, PRAGMA table_info(links) and PRAGMA table_info(clicks) return exactly the columns they return today and no additional tables exist.\n- After driving a key past its quota, the raw key string does not appear in any file under the database directory (including the WAL) and does not appear in any emitted log record.\n- No new HTTP route is added: the OpenAPI paths after the change are exactly /health, /api/links, /api/links/{code}/stats (plus the unlisted /{code}).\n- Every existing test in tests/ passes unchanged after the change.\n\nCONSTRAINTS\n- Python 3 with FastAPI 0.115.6, Starlette 0.41.3, Pydantic 2.10.4; no new runtime dependency may be added to requirements.txt.\n- No SQLite schema change: no new table, column or index; limiter state stays in process memory and is lost on restart.\n- No admin surface: no new route, no runtime mutation of the key set; keys and quotas are read from the process environment only.\n- The environment variable is named exactly SHORTENER_API_KEYS (no LINKS_ prefix), holding comma-separated key:quota pairs.\n- The header is exactly X-API-Key (HTTP header matching is case-insensitive on the name).\n- The quota unit is requests per minute for POST /api/links only.\n- Refusal must use the existing error envelope {\"error\":{\"code\":\"rate_limited\",\"message\":...}} with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header containing whole seconds as a decimal integer, minimum 1.\n- Existing behaviour for unkeyed and unknown-key callers must be byte-for-byte unchanged: same status codes, same buckets, same env var names and defaults (LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX, LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS, LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED, LINKS_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR).\n- Limiting must continue to run as ASGI middleware before routing and body parsing, so a throttled request never opens a database connection.\n- API keys are secrets: they must never be written to SQLite, to a log record, to an exception message or to a response body, and must not be included in the error message returned on 429.\n- Key lookup must not leak the configured key material through a timing side channel that is cheaper than brute forcing the key itself: compare with hmac.compare_digest or look up a salted hash of the presented key rather than doing early-exit string comparison over the configured set.\n- Limiter state must be keyed by a per-boot salted hash of the presented key, matching the existing treatment of client addresses, so no key material sits in memory structures that could be dumped as plaintext keys.\n- The tracked-key map must stay bounded (the existing MAX_TRACKED_KEYS pruning must continue to apply) so an attacker sending random X-API-Key values cannot grow memory without limit; unknown keys must not allocate a per-key bucket at all.\n- Counting must remain thread safe under the existing threading.Lock, because
